scenario: 题目要求“最小成本 / 最大收益 / 最长序列 / 方案数”，暴力枚举会指数爆炸，且许多子问题会重复出现。
scenario_en: The problem asks for minimum cost, maximum gain, longest sequence, or number of ways; brute force explodes exponentially, and many subproblems repeat.
q: 这类信号最应该优先考虑哪种算法模式？
q_en: Which algorithm pattern should you consider first for these signals?
options: 只做一次正则匹配
任意贪心排序
动态规划
LRU Cache
options_en: A single regex match pass
Arbitrary greedy sorting
Dynamic programming (DP)
An LRU cache
why: 优化或计数目标加上重叠子问题，是 DP 的核心信号。先说清状态和递推，再让 AI 处理代码细节。
why_en: Dynamic programming fits optimization or counting problems that have overlapping subproblems.
whenOtherWins: 如果局部最优选择总能保证全局最优，贪心更简单；如果要枚举所有合法配置而不是优化一个值，回溯通常更合适。
tradeoff: 重叠子问题需要状态复用（DP）vs 局部最优可直接提交（贪心）
diagram:
flowchart LR
  Signal[Signal] --> State[State]
  State --> Recurrence[Recurrence]
  Recurrence --> Order[Order]
  Order --> Tests[Tests]

termDefinitions.meaning: 动态规划：把大问题拆成重叠子问题，用状态和递推复用已算过的答案。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Dynamic programming breaks a problem into overlapping subproblems and reuses previously computed answers.

termDefinitions.meaning: 按最近最少使用淘汰旧条目的缓存策略，用来控制内存，不是搜索算法。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An LRU cache evicts the least recently used entry to bound memory and is not a search algorithm.

termDefinitions.meaning: 贪心算法：每一步都选当前看起来最优的选项，不回溯验证。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A greedy algorithm always takes the locally best option without revisiting past choices.

optionExplanations: 正则只能做一次模式匹配，答不出「哪种组合最优」这种最优化问题。
贪心每步只看当前最优，遇到局部最优和全局最优不一致时会选错方向。
有子问题反复出现，又要求最优或计数，正是该用状态和递推复用答案的信号。
LRU 淘汰的是内存里的旧数据，解决不了子问题该怎么组合成最优解。
optionExplanations_en: A single regex pass only locates a pattern; it can't decide which combination is optimal.
Greedy locks in whatever looks best right now, which breaks once a local pick isn't globally optimal.
A problem whose subproblems repeat, combined with an optimize-or-count goal, is the cue to reuse answers via state and recurrence.
An LRU cache evicts old data to bound memory; it has no notion of combining subproblems into an optimum.

scenario: 面试题问“最多能安排多少活动”，n 到 10 万，你要在动手写代码前先判定它是不是 DP。
scenario_en: The interview problem asks for the maximum number of activities you can schedule with n up to a hundred thousand, and you have to decide whether it is DP before writing any code.
q: 在面试里判断一道题该不该上 DP 时，哪些是可靠的识别信号？
q_en: Which are reliable signals that a problem should be solved with DP?
options: 答案是 best X，例如最小、最大、最长、方案数
选择会相互影响，不是独立决定
可以用一句话描述状态，例如“前 i 个元素和预算 j”
暴力搜索有指数级组合但子问题会重复
options_en: The answer is the best X — minimum, maximum, longest, or a count of ways.
Choices compound instead of being decided independently.
The state fits in one sentence, like the first i items with budget j.
Brute force is exponential but the subproblems repeat.
why: 这些信号共同说明问题可以拆成较小状态并复用答案。单独一个信号不一定充分，但组合出现时很强。
why_en: DP signals include an optimal objective, compounding choices, a clean state, and repeated exponential subproblems.
optionExplanations: 问的是一个最优值或计数，而不是任意可行解，这类目标天然适合用 DP 求解。
选择互相牵连时不能贪心地孤立决定每一步，需要状态记录之前的选择结果。
状态能压成一句话说明白，就有了 DP 表格该怎么设计行列的起点。
组合数量指数增长但子问题重复出现，说明缓存中间结果能把复杂度降下来。
optionExplanations_en: Asking for one optimal value or a count, not just any feasible answer, is a shape DP naturally fits.
When choices depend on earlier ones, you can't decide each step in isolation — you need state to remember the past.
Being able to name the state in one sentence gives you the starting point for the table's rows and columns.
Exponential combinations with repeating subproblems is the classic case where caching intermediate results collapses the cost.

scenario: 同一道“最少硬币找零”题，币值是任意集合而不是标准面额，你要选 DP 还是贪心。
scenario_en: In the same coin-change problem the denominations are an arbitrary set rather than standard ones, and you have to pick between DP and greedy.
q: 判断该用 DP 还是贪心（Greedy）时，最有用的自检问题是什么？
q_en: When choosing between DP and greedy, what is the most useful self-check?
options: 代码是否用了两层 for 循环？
当前最好的选择会不会让后面错过更优答案？
输入是否包含字符串？
最终时间复杂度是否正好是 O(n²)？
options_en: Does the code use a nested for loop?
Could the locally best-looking choice cause you to miss a better answer later?
Does the input contain a string?
Is the final time complexity exactly O(n squared)?
why: 如果局部选择可能把未来锁死，就需要 DP 或其他全局方法；若局部最优能安全提交，贪心更简单更快。
why_en: If a locally best choice can block a better future outcome, greedy is suspect and DP may be needed.
tradeoff: DP：状态穷举保证全局最优，设计成本高 vs 贪心：一步到位，简单快，但前提未证明就可能错

termDefinitions.meaning: 动态规划：用状态和递推穷举并复用子问题答案，保证找到全局最优。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Dynamic programming enumerates and reuses subproblem answers via state and recurrence to guarantee a global optimum.

termDefinitions.meaning: 贪心算法：每一步都选当前最优，不回头验证，只有在局部最优等于全局最优时才正确。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A greedy algorithm always takes the current best option without revisiting it, and is only correct when local optimum equals global optimum.

optionExplanations: 循环嵌套几层是实现细节，贪心和 DP 写法都可能用两层循环，分不出算法类型。
这句正是 DP 与贪心的分界线：局部最优可能锁死后面的更优解，就该转向 DP。
字符串题里一样有大量贪心问题，输入类型判断不了要不要做全局搜索。
复杂度是结果不是原因，同一个 O(n²) 背后可能是完全不同的算法。
optionExplanations_en: Loop nesting is an implementation detail — both greedy and DP code can use two nested loops, so it can't tell them apart.
This is the real DP-vs-greedy line: if a locally best pick can block a better answer later, you need DP.
Plenty of greedy problems also involve strings, so input type says nothing about whether global search is required.
Complexity is an outcome, not a cause — the same O(n squared) can come from very different algorithms.

q: 填空：一个 DP 解法的四个组成部分。
q_en: Fill in the four parts of a DP solution.
text: DP 需要定义{{状态}}、{{递推关系}}、{{base cases}}、以及{{求值顺序}}。
why: 状态说明表格每个格子是什么意思；没有状态就无法可靠写递推。AI 可以帮你落代码，但这四件事要由你验证。
why_en: A DP solution is built from state, recurrence, base cases, and evaluation order.

termDefinitions.meaning: 递推的边界值，不靠推导直接写死的最小子问题答案。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A base case is the smallest subproblem's answer, written down directly rather than derived.

termDefinitions.meaning: DP 表格里一个格子代表的具体含义，例如“前 i 个元素、预算 j 时的最优值”。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The state is what one table cell means, such as the best value using the first i items with budget j.

scenario: 爬楼梯每次只能走 1 或 2 阶，面试官要你讲清递推是怎么推出来的，而不是背公式。
scenario_en: In climbing stairs you can take one or two steps at a time, and the interviewer wants you to explain how the recurrence is derived rather than recite it.
q: 爬楼梯问题中，`ways[n] = ways[n-1] + ways[n-2]` 的直觉是什么？
q_en: In climbing stairs, what is the intuition behind ways[n] = ways[n-1] + ways[n-2]?
options: 最后一步只能来自 n-1 或 n-2，两者不重叠
每一步都必须先跳 1 阶、再跳 2 阶，顺序固定
所有到达第 n 阶的路径长度都相等
递推只是为了让数组长度和 n 对齐
options_en: The last move can only come from step n-1 or n-2, and the two cases never overlap.
Every path must take a 1-step first and a 2-step second, in that fixed order.
Every path that reaches step n has the same number of moves.
The recurrence only exists to size the array to n.
why: 最后一步分类覆盖全部情况且互不重叠，所以总数相加。这个“从最后一步反推”是很多 DP 递推的来源。
why_en: The recurrence comes from partitioning paths by whether the last move was one step or two steps.
diagram:
flowchart LR
  W0[ways 0] --> W2[ways 2]
  W1[ways 1] --> W2
  W1 --> W3[ways 3]
  W2 --> W3
optionExplanations: 按最后一步是 1 阶还是 2 阶，把路径分成两组互不重叠的集合，加起来正好是总数。
实际走法里 1 阶和 2 阶能任意顺序组合，把它当成固定顺序会漏掉绝大多数路径。
路径的步数其实从全 1 阶的 n 步到全 2 阶的约 n/2 步都有，长度并不恒定。
递推公式是加法这件事来自组合计数，不是为了凑数组长度而写的技巧。
optionExplanations_en: Splitting every path by whether its last move was 1 or 2 steps gives two non-overlapping groups whose counts simply add up.
Real paths mix 1-steps and 2-steps in any order, so treating it as one fixed sequence drops most valid paths.
Path length actually ranges from n moves (all 1-steps) down to about n/2 (all 2-steps) — it isn't constant.
The addition in the recurrence comes from counting combinations, not a trick to size the array.

scenario: 面试要求爬楼梯函数处理 n 到几万级别，朴素递归 `ways(n) = ways(n-1) + ways(n-2)` 在大 n 下会超时。
scenario_en: The interview asks the climbing-stairs function to handle n in the tens of thousands, and the naive recursion ways(n) = ways(n-1) + ways(n-2) times out for large n.
q: 把朴素递归换成 memo 或自底向上表格后，复杂度为什么能从 O(2ⁿ) 降到 O(n)？
q_en: Why does memoization or bottom-up tabulation reduce the complexity from O(2^n) to O(n)?
options: 递归完全消失了所有循环，所以自动变快
缓存或自底向上填表后，每个不同的 i 只计算一次
因为运行时会自动缓存并合并所有重复的递归调用
因为爬楼梯的答案总是等于 1
options_en: Recursion removes all loops, so it automatically speeds up.
Caching or bottom-up filling means each distinct i is computed only once.
Because the runtime automatically caches and merges every duplicate recursive call.
Because the climbing-stairs answer is always 1.
why: 朴素递归里 ways(3)、ways(2) 等相同子问题被反复算：公式是子问题数 = n（i 从 0 到 n），memo/tabulation 把每个状态从多次调用压到一次。这个 n 是后续估算面试代码是否会超时的依据。
why_en: Memoization or tabulation reduces exponential recursion by computing each of the n distinct states exactly once.
diagram:
flowchart TD
  Call[ways n] --> A[ways n-1]
  Call --> B[ways n-2]
  A --> Seen[cache hit]
  B --> Seen

termDefinitions.meaning: 递归时把已经算过的子问题结果存起来，下次遇到直接返回缓存值。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Memoization stores the result of a subproblem the first time it is computed and returns the cached value on repeat calls.

termDefinitions.meaning: 自底向上填表：从最小的子问题开始，按依赖顺序逐个算到目标状态。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Tabulation fills a table bottom-up, computing each state in dependency order from the smallest subproblem to the target.

termDefinitions.meaning: 指数级复杂度：每多一层递归分支数量翻倍，n 稍大就会超时。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: O(2 to the n) is exponential complexity where the branch count doubles with each extra level, timing out for even moderate n.

optionExplanations: 递归换成循环并不会自动变快，真正提速的是避免重复计算同一个子问题。
缓存或按依赖顺序填表后，每个不同的 i 只会被算一次，指数分支被压平成 n 个状态。
运行时不会替你识别并合并重复的递归调用，需要显式的 memo 或表格才行。
爬楼梯的答案随 n 增长（1,2,3,5,8…），不是恒定值，这个说法本身就错了。
optionExplanations_en: Swapping recursion for loops doesn't speed things up by itself — the fix is not recomputing the same subproblem.
Caching or filling the table in dependency order computes each distinct i once, flattening the branches into n states.
The runtime doesn't automatically detect and merge duplicate recursive calls — that needs an explicit memo or table.
The climbing-stairs count grows with n (1, 2, 3, 5, 8...), so it's never fixed — this claim is simply false.

q: 填空：爬楼梯的 base cases。
q_en: Fill in the base cases for climbing stairs.
text: 爬楼梯中，`ways[0] = {{1}}` 表示不动也算一种方式，`ways[1] = {{1}}` 表示只能走一步。
why: base case 是递推的底部，不是循环里推出来的。很多 DP bug 都来自这些边界值被写错。
why_en: The base cases anchor the recurrence before any table-filling begins.

termDefinitions.meaning: 递推链条的起点，直接给定而不是由更小状态算出来的值。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A base case is the starting value of the recurrence chain, given directly rather than derived from a smaller state.

scenario: AI 已经把爬楼梯的状态 `ways[i]` 和递推 `ways[i] = ways[i-1] + ways[i-2]` 写进了下面的自底向上实现，你在审查循环部分。
scenario_en: The AI has already put the climbing-stairs state ways[i] and recurrence ways[i] = ways[i-1] + ways[i-2] into this bottom-up implementation, and you are reviewing the loop.
q: 这段爬楼梯代码里的 `for i in range(2, n + 1)` 表示 DP 的哪一部分？
q_en: In this climbing-stairs code, which part of DP does for i in range(2, n + 1) represent?
codeSample:
ways[0] = 1
ways[1] = 1
for i in range(2, n + 1):
    ways[i] = ways[i - 1] + ways[i - 2]
options: 状态定义：每个格子的含义
哈希表扩容
求值顺序：从小状态到大状态
图的入度更新
options_en: The state definition: what each cell means
Hash table resizing
The evaluation order: fill small states before large ones
Updating in-degrees in a graph
why: 每个 `ways[i]` 依赖前两个位置，所以必须从左到右填。求值顺序保证读到的依赖已经计算完成。
why_en: The loop is the evaluation order that fills states only after their dependencies exist.
optionExplanations: 状态定义是一句语义描述（`ways[i]` 表示什么），不是循环这行代码本身。
DP 数组按下标直接寻址，没有哈希冲突或扩容的概念，套用不上。
循环从小 i 走到大 i，保证每个格子被写入时它依赖的前两个格子已经算好。
爬楼梯是线性递推，没有图结构也没有入度这个概念可言。
optionExplanations_en: The state definition is the sentence explaining what ways[i] means, not the loop line itself.
A DP array is addressed directly by index; there's no hashing or resizing concept to apply here.
Walking from small i to large i guarantees each cell's two dependencies are already filled before it's written.
Climbing stairs is a linear recurrence with no graph structure, so there's no in-degree to speak of.

scenario: 你要让 AI 实现 edit distance，但不想把所有索引和 base case 都手写成伪代码。
scenario_en: You want the AI to implement edit distance, but you do not want to handwrite every index and base case as pseudocode.
q: 哪个提示最接近文章说的“刚刚好”？
q_en: Which prompt is closest to the article's just-right level of detail?
options: 实现 edit distance
用自底向上 DP；状态是两个字符串前缀的二维表，插入、删除、替换成本都为 1
逐字指定所有循环边界、每个 base case 和 return cell
随便写一个字符串相似度算法
options_en: Implement edit distance.
Use bottom-up DP; the state is a 2D table over prefixes of both strings, with insert, delete, and replace each costing 1.
Spell out every loop bound, each base case, and return cell by hand.
Just write some string-similarity algorithm.
why: 好提示给出模式、维度和成本模型，但不把索引细节完全锁死。这样你还有明确结构可验证，AI 也能处理机械实现。
why_en: A just-right DP prompt states the pattern, dimensions, and cost model without transcribing every index.
whenOtherWins: 如果题目约束很特殊，可能需要更具体地指定状态或操作；如果只是探索算法，可以先让 AI 提建议再收敛。
tradeoff: 太模糊（AI 替你决策）vs 太具体（AI 只是抄写员）；“刚刚好”在两者之间点名模式和维度

termDefinitions.meaning: 把一个字符串变成另一个所需要的最少插入、删除、替换次数。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Edit distance is the minimum number of insertions, deletions, and replacements needed to turn one string into another.

optionExplanations: 只说目标会把状态设计的决定权交给 AI，猜错了你就在调试一个自己没做过的方案。
点名模式、维度和成本模型但不锁死索引，你有可验证的结构，AI 能处理机械细节。
把索引、base case、return cell 全写成伪代码，AI 变成转录员，你的笔误会被原样执行。
没点名是 DP 也没给成本模型，AI 可能套用相邻的 LCS 之类模板而不是 edit distance。
optionExplanations_en: Stating only the goal hands state design to the AI — guess wrong and you're debugging a plan you never made.
Naming the pattern, dimensions, and cost model without pinning every index gives you a checkable structure.
Spelling out every index and base case as pseudocode turns the AI into a transcriber that ships your typos.
Without naming DP or a cost model, the AI might borrow a neighboring template like LCS instead of edit distance.

scenario: AI 编码面试给 35 分钟做一道 DP 题，允许用 AI 写代码，评分看你的判断而不是打字量。
scenario_en: An AI-assisted coding interview gives you 35 minutes on a DP problem; using AI is allowed, so the score rides on your judgment, not your typing.
q: DP 题里，哪些工作更应该由你主导而不是直接外包给 AI？
q_en: In a DP interview problem, which work should you own instead of outsourcing directly to AI?
options: 识别这是 DP
用自然语言定义状态
说出 base cases 和核心测试
让 AI 处理变量名、数组大小和循环代码
options_en: Recognizing that this is DP
Defining the state in plain language
Naming the base cases and the core tests
Letting the AI handle variable names, array sizes, and loop code
why: 面试官主要看你能否找对状态和验证边界。AI 很适合把已定的状态和递推翻译成代码。
why_en: You should own recognition, state definition, and base cases while the AI can handle mechanical implementation.
optionExplanations: 听出产品包装下的重叠子问题＋最优目标信号，是面试官评估你的第一关，不能外包。
用一句话说清每个格子的含义，是判断 base case、递推对不对的前提，只有你能做。
边界值和几个手推例子是验证 AI 输出的凭据，说不出这些就没法判断代码对不对。
变量名、数组大小、循环代码是机械转写，AI 做得又快又准，不需要你逐行盯着。
optionExplanations_en: Hearing the overlapping-subproblems-plus-optimal-goal signal under a wrapper is what the interviewer grades first.
Stating in one sentence what each cell means is the prerequisite for judging the base cases and recurrence.
Boundary values and a couple of hand-traced examples are the evidence used to check the AI's output.
Variable names, array sizes, and loop code are mechanical work the AI handles fast and accurately on its own.

scenario: 你在 AI 编码面试里只对模型说了一句“implement edit distance”或“fix the bug”，没有给出状态、维度或成本模型。
scenario_en: In an AI coding interview, you only tell the model implement edit distance or fix the bug, without giving the state, dimensions, or cost model.
q: 这种过于模糊的 DP 提示，主要风险是什么？
q_en: What is the main risk of this overly vague DP prompt?
options: 所有隐藏测试都会自动帮你覆盖这个边界情况
AI 会挑一个默认状态，你可能在调试自己没设计的方案
代码逻辑一定会自动退化成贪心算法
AI 遇到模糊提示时会直接报错并拒绝生成任何代码
options_en: All hidden tests will automatically cover this edge case for you.
The AI picks a default state and recurrence, leaving you debugging a design you never made.
The code logic will automatically degrade into a greedy algorithm.
The AI will just error out and refuse to generate any code when a prompt is vague.
why: 如果默认假设不符合题意，你会在面试中解释不了维度、base case 或递推来源。模糊提示削弱的是你的控制力。
why_en: A vague DP prompt lets the AI choose the state and recurrence, leaving you unable to defend the solution.
optionExplanations: 提示模糊不会让隐藏测试自动变多，边界覆盖仍然要靠你自己写测试。
AI 会替你挑一个默认状态和递推，面试官问“为什么是二维表”时你答不出来，因为选择不是你做的。
模糊提示更可能让 AI 选错 DP 的具体形状，而不是整体退化成另一个算法族。
AI 遇到模糊提示通常还是会热心给出一个能跑的实现，只是不一定是你要的那个。
optionExplanations_en: A vague prompt doesn't magically add hidden-test coverage — edge cases still need tests you write yourself.
The AI picks a default state and recurrence for you, so you can't defend why the table is 2D — you never chose it.
A vague prompt is more likely to make the AI pick the wrong DP shape than switch it to another algorithm family.
Faced with a vague prompt, the AI usually still produces something runnable — just not the design you intended.

scenario: 你把 DP 提示写成了完整伪代码：所有循环边界、base case 公式和 return cell 都逐字指定给 AI。
scenario_en: You write the DP prompt as complete pseudocode, specifying every loop bound, base-case formula, and return cell for the AI.
q: 这种过于具体的提示，有什么风险？
q_en: What is the risk of this overly specific prompt?
options: 如果你的某个细节错了，AI 会忠实实现这个 bug
AI 会自动帮你验证并证明整个算法完全正确无误
生成出来的代码一定天生更容易验证
状态定义从此可以完全跳过，不用再写
options_en: If one of your details is wrong, the AI will faithfully implement that bug.
The AI will automatically verify and prove the whole algorithm completely correct.
The generated code is inherently easier to verify.
State definition can be skipped entirely from now on.
why: 过度具体会把 AI 变成抄写器。你写错 base case 或 return cell，它不会知道你本意是什么。
why_en: An over-specific prompt can make the AI faithfully implement your mistaken indices or base cases.
optionExplanations: 提示写成完整伪代码后，AI 变成转录员，会把你笔误的索引或边界值原样实现成 bug。
AI 不会主动质疑你给出的公式对不对，它默认你是对的，不会自己去证明正确性。
代码是否好验证取决于测试和手推例子，和提示写得多详细没有关系。
提示够具体不代表状态语义就自动正确，base case 和 return cell 仍然要靠人确认。
optionExplanations_en: Once the prompt is complete pseudocode, the AI becomes a transcriber — your mistaken base case gets built exactly as written.
The AI doesn't question the formula you handed it; it assumes you're right rather than proving correctness itself.
How easy code is to verify depends on tests and hand-traced examples, not on how detailed the prompt was.
A detailed prompt doesn't make the state semantics automatically correct — a human still has to confirm them.

scenario: 你准备提示 AI 写 DP 代码，但还没实现任何东西。
scenario_en: You are about to prompt the AI to write DP code, but you have not implemented anything yet.
q: 在提示 AI 之前，最值得先做的事是什么？
q_en: What is the most valuable thing to do before prompting the AI?
options: 只跑一次最大规模输入看性能
等代码生成后再猜 base case
不写测试，直接读完整张表
先写几个小测试和边界测试，锁定期望答案
options_en: Run only the largest-scale input once to check performance.
Wait until the code is generated, then guess the base cases.
Skip tests and read the entire table directly.
Write a few small and edge-case tests first to pin down the expected answers.
why: 测试会逼你思考 base case，也给 AI 输出一个可验证目标。DP 的空字符串、相等字符串、单字符等边界特别容易错。
why_en: Writing tests before prompting pins down DP base cases and gives the AI output something concrete to prove.
whenOtherWins: 如果题目还没理解清楚，可以先手推一个小例子；但很快应把它转成测试。
tradeoff: 先写测试再提示（多几分钟但有验证目标）vs 直接提示（省时间但没有可核对的基准）
optionExplanations: 只跑一次最大规模输入能看出性能，但看不出空串、单字符这些容易出错的正确性边界。
先有代码再猜 base case 是本末倒置，之后很难判断 AI 给的边界值到底对不对。
DP 表格常有几十上百格，靠肉眼通读来找 bug 在面试压力下不现实。
先写几个小测试和边界用例，把期望结果钉死，AI 生成的代码就有了具体的核对基准。
optionExplanations_en: Running only the largest input once shows performance but misses correctness edges like empty or one-char strings.
Guessing base cases after the code exists puts the cart before the horse — you can't judge the AI's boundary values later.
A DP table often has dozens of cells; eyeballing the whole thing for bugs isn't realistic under interview pressure.
Writing a few small and edge-case tests first forces you to pin down base cases and gives the AI a checkable target.

scenario: 拼写纠错要从字典中找和输入词最接近的词，距离按插入、删除、替换字符数计算。
scenario_en: A spell checker must find the closest dictionary word to the input word, where distance is counted by insertions, deletions, and replacements.
q: 解决“最接近的词”这个核心子问题，应该用哪种算法？
q_en: Which algorithm should solve the core closest-word subproblem?
options: 基于 LRU 最近最少使用的缓存淘汰策略
Edit distance 的二维 DP
有向图的拓扑排序
只按字符串长度做排序比较
options_en: An LRU (least recently used) cache eviction policy
The 2D edit-distance DP
Topological sort on a directed graph
Comparing candidates only by string length
why: 两个字符串、三种编辑操作、求最小操作数，是 edit distance 的标准形状。外层可以遍历候选词，核心距离用 DP 算。
why_en: Spell-check closeness by single-character edits is the classic edit-distance DP.
whenOtherWins: 如果只是固定模式查找，KMP、trie 或正则可能更合适；edit distance 用于允许模糊编辑的相似度。
tradeoff: 允许模糊编辑求最小代价（edit distance DP）vs 只做精确/固定模式匹配（trie、KMP）
diagram:
flowchart LR
  Empty[empty prefix] --> Row[base row]
  Empty --> Col[base col]
  Row --> Cell[dp i j]
  Col --> Cell
  Cell --> Answer[dp m n]

termDefinitions.meaning: 把一个字符串变成另一个所需要的最少插入、删除、替换次数。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Edit distance is the minimum number of insertions, deletions, and replacements needed to turn one string into another.

termDefinitions.meaning: 一种线性时间的精确子串匹配算法，不处理模糊编辑。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: KMP is a linear-time exact substring matching algorithm that does not handle fuzzy edits.

termDefinitions.meaning: 前缀树：按公共前缀组织字符串的树形结构，适合精确前缀查找。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A trie is a tree that organizes strings by shared prefixes, suited to exact prefix lookups.

optionExplanations: LRU 是缓存淘汰策略，管的是内存该留谁，不衡量两个词有多接近。
两个字符串前缀的二维表，能精确算出把一个词变成另一个词的最少编辑次数，直接支撑“最接近”。
拓扑排序给有依赖关系的节点排顺序，候选词之间没有这种依赖，用不上。
长度接近的词编辑距离不一定小，比如替换和插入代价不同，长度排序会漏掉真正相近的词。
optionExplanations_en: An LRU cache is an eviction policy about what to keep in memory; it never measures how close two words are.
A 2D table over both strings' prefixes computes the exact minimum edit count between them — exactly what closeness means here.
Topological sort orders nodes that depend on each other; candidate words here have no such dependency.
Similar-length words aren't necessarily close in edits since insert and replace cost differently, so length sorting misses close words.

q: 填空：Edit distance 的状态定义。
q_en: Fill in the state definition for edit distance.
text: `dp[i][j]` 表示把第一个字符串的{{前 i 个字符}}变成第二个字符串的{{前 j 个字符}}所需的最少编辑次数。
why: 这个状态定义直接解释了为什么需要二维表：两个前缀长度各占一个维度。后续 base case 和递推都从它推出。
why_en: Edit-distance state is the minimum edits between prefixes of lengths i and j.

scenario: 你定义 `dp[i][j]` 为 s 前 i 个字符变成 t 前 j 个字符的最小编辑次数，现在要填第 0 行和第 0 列。
scenario_en: You define dp[i][j] as the minimum edits to turn the first i characters of s into the first j characters of t, and now you have to fill row zero and column zero.
q: Edit distance 的边界行列应该如何理解？
q_en: How should you understand the border row and column in edit distance?
options: `dp[0][j] = j`，空串变成长度 j 的前缀需要 j 次插入
`dp[i][0] = i`，长度 i 的前缀变成空串需要 i 次删除
`dp[0][j]` 全部为 0，因为空串不需要操作
`dp[i][0]` 全部为 1，因为只删一次
options_en: dp[0][j] = j: turning an empty string into a length-j prefix takes j insertions.
dp[i][0] = i: turning a length-i prefix into an empty string takes i deletions.
dp[0][j] is always 0 because an empty string needs no operations.
dp[i][0] is always 1 because it only takes one delete.
why: 边界值可以直接从状态语义看出来，不需要递推。它们也是最常见的 off-by-one bug 来源。
why_en: The edit-distance borders count insertions from empty and deletions to empty.
optionExplanations: 空串变成长度 j 的前缀，只能靠插入，所以 `dp[0][j]` 直接等于插入次数 j。
长度 i 的前缀变成空串，只能靠删除，所以 `dp[i][0]` 直接等于删除次数 i。
只有 `dp[0][0]` 才是 0；一旦 j>0，空串到非空前缀仍然需要 j 次插入，不会是 0。
把删除次数误当成固定的 1，忽略了要删的其实是整整 i 个字符。
optionExplanations_en: Turning an empty string into a length-j prefix takes only insertions, so dp[0][j] equals j directly.
Turning a length-i prefix into an empty string takes only deletions, so dp[i][0] equals i directly.
Only dp[0][0] is 0; once j is greater than 0, empty to a non-empty prefix still needs j insertions, not 0.
Treating the delete count as a fixed 1 ignores that there are actually i whole characters to delete.

scenario: 同一张 edit distance 表里，替换、删除、插入代价都是 1，你正在填一个内部格子 `dp[i][j]`。
scenario_en: In the same edit-distance table, substitution, deletion, and insertion each cost one, and you are filling an inner cell dp[i][j].
q: Edit distance 内部格子的递推核心是什么？
q_en: What is the core recurrence for an inner edit-distance cell?
options: 不管字符是否相等，永远取上方格子
相等复制左上角；不等则替换/删除/插入取最小加一
不管字符是否相等，永远取左方格子的值再加 2
字符相等时也必须额外加 1 的代价
options_en: Always take the cell above, regardless of whether the characters match.
On a match, copy the diagonal; otherwise take one plus the minimum of replace, delete, or insert.
Always take the value in the cell to the left and add 2, regardless of match.
Even a matching character must add an extra cost of 1.
why: 左上、上方、左方分别对应替换、删除、插入。字符已经相等时不需要额外编辑，直接继承左上角。
why_en: Edit distance copies the diagonal on a match and otherwise takes one plus the cheapest replace, delete, or insert predecessor.
diagram:
flowchart TD
  Up[delete] --> Min[min plus 1]
  Left[insert] --> Min
  Diag[replace] --> Min
  Same[same char] --> Copy[copy diag]
optionExplanations: 只取上方格子等于只考虑删除操作，会漏掉替换和插入更便宜的情况，结果偏大或直接错。
字符相等就复制左上角，不等就在替换/删除/插入三者里取最小值加一，覆盖了全部情况。
凭空在左方格子上加 2，这个规则不对应任何真实的编辑操作。
字符已经相等就不该再计一次编辑，如果每个匹配字符都多算一次，最终距离会比真实值大。
optionExplanations_en: Always taking the cell above only accounts for deletion, missing cheaper replace/insert cases, so the result comes out wrong.
On a match, copy the diagonal; on a mismatch, take one plus the cheapest of replace, delete, or insert — covers every case.
Adding an unexplained 2 to the left cell corresponds to no real edit operation.
A matching character shouldn't cost anything; charging one for every match makes the final distance too large.

scenario: AI 已经按“字符相等复制左上角、不等取三者最小值加一”的递推写出了下面这段 edit distance 内层代码，你在检查匹配分支。
scenario_en: The AI has written the edit-distance inner loop using copy diagonal on a match and one plus the minimum of three choices on a mismatch; you are checking the match branch.
q: 这段 edit distance 的分支中，`dp[i - 1][j - 1]` 在字符相等时代表什么？
q_en: In this edit-distance branch, what does dp[i - 1][j - 1] mean when the characters match?
options: 当前这一对已经匹配的字符必须替换掉的成本
哈希表的冲突次数统计
去掉当前两个相同字符后，两个前缀的最优编辑数
整张 dp 表格里的最大值
options_en: The cost of replacing this already-matching pair of characters.
A tally of hash collisions inside a hash table.
The optimal edit count for the two prefixes with the current matching characters removed.
The maximum value across the whole dp table.
why: 当前字符相等时不用编辑它们，问题退化为对齐前面的两个前缀。这个分支是检查递推正确性的重点。
why_en: On a character match, the cost is exactly the diagonal subproblem for the previous prefixes.
optionExplanations: 代码在字符相等分支里根本没有加 1，说明这里没有付出替换成本。
DP 数组是按下标寻址的表格，不存在哈希冲突这个概念，套用不上。
字符相等时不用再编辑它们，问题退化成去掉这对字符后剩余前缀的最优编辑数。
每个格子只对应它自己的一对前缀，整张表不是在维护一个全局最大值。
optionExplanations_en: The match branch adds no 1 in the code, so no replace cost is actually charged here.
A DP array is addressed by index; there's no hash-collision concept to apply here.
When characters match there's nothing left to edit — it reduces to the optimal count for the prefixes with that pair removed.
Each cell belongs to its own pair of prefixes; the table isn't tracking a single running maximum.

q: 把 edit distance 的推导顺序排好。
q_en: Put the edit-distance derivation steps in order.
steps: 说出 base cases：空串到前缀是插入，前缀到空串是删除。
定义状态：两个字符串前缀之间的最少编辑数。
用一个小例子如 KATE 到 SAT 手算答案 2。
描述递推：相等取左上，不等取插入/删除/替换的最小值加 1。
提示 AI 写 bottom-up 代码，再用测试和表格验证。
why: 先用具体例子确认语义，再抽象成状态、边界和递推。这样 AI 输出有明确的验证依据。
why_en: A strong edit-distance derivation moves from a tiny example to state, base cases, recurrence, and AI-assisted implementation.
tradeoff: 先手推例子再抽象（多两分钟但有验证基准）vs 直接抽象定义（省时间但没有可核对的具体答案）

termDefinitions.meaning: 自底向上：从最小子问题开始按依赖顺序填表，不使用递归调用栈。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Bottom-up fills the table from the smallest subproblem in dependency order, without a recursive call stack.

scenario: AI 生成了 DP 代码，你不想逐行盯所有索引，但需要快速验证递推和边界。
scenario_en: The AI generated DP code, and you need to quickly verify the recurrence and borders without staring at every index.
q: 文章推荐的高杠杆调试提示是什么？
q_en: What high-leverage debugging prompt does the article recommend?
options: 只盯着函数最后一行的变量名反复对照
让 AI 打印小输入的完整 dp 表，核对手推的几个格子
不看任何中间输出，直接删掉所有测试用例
不做任何验证，直接把整个 DP 全部推倒换成贪心重写
options_en: Only stare repeatedly at the variable names on the function's last line.
Ask the AI to print the full dp table for a small input, then check it against a few hand-traced cells.
Skip every intermediate output and delete all the test cases outright.
Skip verification entirely and tear down the whole DP to rewrite it as greedy instead.
why: 打印表格能把隐藏在循环里的错误变成可观察状态。先对照左上 2x2，就能定位 base case 或递推问题。
why_en: Printing a small DP table makes base-case and recurrence bugs visible without reading every loop expression.
whenOtherWins: 如果代码很短且你已经很熟悉，也可以直接读循环；但表格验证在面试压力下更稳。
tradeoff: 打印表格核对（多一步但错误可定位）vs 直接读循环代码（省步骤但压力下容易漏看）
optionExplanations: 只看返回值那一行看不出中间格子或 base case 是不是算错了。
打印小输入的完整表格，对照左上 2x2 手推，base case 错在首行首列露出来，递推错在第一个内部格子露出来。
删掉测试只会让验证更难，bug 只能靠肉眼通读代码去猜，反而更慢。
换成贪心解决不了当前 DP 实现是否正确的问题，而且贪心不一定适用这道题。
optionExplanations_en: Looking only at the returned line reveals nothing about whether an intermediate cell was computed wrong.
Printing the small table and checking a hand-traced 2x2 shows a base-case bug in row/column one, a recurrence bug in the first inner cell.
Deleting the tests only makes verification harder, leaving you to guess at bugs by reading code instead.
Switching to greedy doesn't verify whether the current DP is correct, and greedy may not even fit this problem.

scenario: AI 刚写完 edit distance，你只剩 2 分钟做正确性验证，必须挑答案已知的小用例。
scenario_en: The AI has just finished edit distance and you have only two minutes to verify correctness, so you need small cases whose answers you already know.
q: 验证 edit distance 时，哪些测试很有价值？
q_en: Which tests are valuable for verifying edit distance?
options: 两个相同字符串应返回 0
空串到 `abc` 应返回 3
`kate` 到 `sat` 应返回 2
只测试一个很长随机字符串且不知道答案
options_en: Two identical strings should return 0.
Empty string to 'abc' should return 3.
'kate' to 'sat' should return 2.
Testing only one long random string with an unknown expected answer.
why: 这些小测试分别覆盖相等、边界行列和非平凡递推。未知答案的大随机输入不适合作为第一轮正确性验证。
why_en: Good DP tests include equal inputs, empty-prefix cases, and a small hand-computed nontrivial case.
optionExplanations: 两个字符串完全相同时编辑距离该是 0，这是最基础也最容易先验证的用例。
空串到三字符的距离该是 3，专门验证边界初始化（`dp[0][j]=j`）对不对。
kate 到 sat 是一个非平凡的手算例子，能同时检验替换/删除/插入三条路径的递推。
一个连答案都不知道的大随机输入，测试通过或失败都没法归因到具体哪一步错了。
optionExplanations_en: Two identical strings should give distance 0 — the simplest and easiest case to verify first.
Empty string to a three-character word should give 3, checking whether the border dp[0][j] = j is right.
kate to sat is a small nontrivial hand-computed case that exercises replace, delete, and insert together.
A large random input with no known answer gives no baseline — a pass or fail can't be traced to any step.

scenario: 一个 DP 测试失败了，你正准备把报错信息发给 AI。
scenario_en: A DP test failed, and you are about to send the error output to the AI.
q: 为什么不该只把报错扔给 AI 说“修一下”？
q_en: Why should you not just throw an error at the AI and say fix it?
options: 所有隐藏测试都会自动覆盖这个具体边界
DP 代码天生正确，永远不需要调试
先形成具体假设，再带着假设去提示 AI
AI 完全无法读取或理解测试失败信息
options_en: Every hidden test will automatically cover this specific edge.
DP code is inherently correct and never needs debugging.
Form a hypothesis first, such as an off-by-one base case, then prompt the AI with it.
The AI is entirely unable to read or understand test-failure output.
why: 带假设的提示证明你仍在控制调试方向，也能防止 AI 盲目重写整个方案。面试官会看到你的定位能力。
why_en: When a DP test fails, prompt with a concrete hypothesis so the AI fixes the suspected structure rather than thrashing.
optionExplanations: 测试覆盖率是写测试时就定好的，和现在该怎么提示 AI 修 bug 是两回事。
DP 代码和其他代码一样会有 bug，一样需要调试，只是调试方式要讲究方法。
先自己定位可能出错的结构（比如某个 base case 差一），带着这个假设提示 AI，能防止它盲目重写整个方案。
AI 完全读得懂报错和期望/实际值的差异，它缺的是往哪个方向改的线索，不是能力。
optionExplanations_en: Test coverage was decided when the tests were written; it's unrelated to how you prompt a fix right now.
DP code has bugs like any other code and needs debugging the same way, just guided by a clear hypothesis.
Forming a hypothesis first — say, an off-by-one base case — keeps the AI's fix targeted instead of a blind rewrite.
The AI can read the error and the expected-vs-actual gap fine; what it's missing is direction, not the ability.

scenario: AI 生成的 DP 代码能跑，但样例输出偏小，你要按结构位置逐项排查而不是逐行读代码。
scenario_en: AI-generated DP code runs but returns a value that is too small on the sample, and you want to check it by structural location instead of reading line by line.
q: DP bug 最常住在哪些结构位置？
q_en: Where do DP bugs most often live structurally?
options: base cases
递推表达式
遍历顺序
返回的格子或状态
options_en: The base cases
The recurrence expression
The traversal order
The returned cell or state
why: DP 代码表面相似，错误通常是结构性的一个格子、一条边或一个循环方向。审查时按这四处逐项过。
why_en: DP bugs concentrate in base cases, recurrence, traversal order, and return state.
optionExplanations: base case 是递推的起点，写错一个边界值，整张表从第一格就偏了。
递推表达式选错分支或漏掉一条转移路径，算出来的数值直接就是错的。
遍历顺序反了，`ways[i-1]` 这类依赖会读到还没算出来的值。
表格全填对了，但返回了相邻子问题的格子，输出照样是错的。
optionExplanations_en: A base case anchors the recurrence; get one boundary value wrong and the table is off from the first cell.
Picking the wrong branch or dropping a transition in the recurrence directly produces a wrong number.
Reversing the traversal order means a dependency like ways[i-1] gets read before it's written.
The table can be entirely correct yet still return a neighboring cell instead of the real answer.

scenario: 你让 AI 写 longest palindromic substring，它给回的表格形状很像 edit distance，本地样例全过。
scenario_en: You ask the AI for longest palindromic substring, and it hands back a table shaped a lot like edit distance that passes every local sample.
q: 能跑、也过了样例的 DP 递推，为什么反而特别危险？
q_en: Why is a DP recurrence that runs and passes the samples especially dangerous?
options: 这种代码一定会编译失败
这种问题只会影响代码风格
类型检查器总能自动发现这种语义错误
AI 可能套用了相邻问题的错误递推模板
options_en: Code like this is guaranteed to fail to compile.
A problem like this only affects code style.
The type checker will always catch this kind of semantic error automatically.
The AI may have borrowed the wrong recurrence template from a neighboring problem.
why: 相邻 DP 题的表格形状很像，但递推语义不同。代码能跑、简单测试也可能过，隐藏测试才会暴露。
why_en: Almost-right recurrences are dangerous because neighboring DP problems can share table shapes but need different transitions.

termDefinitions.meaning: 最长公共子序列：两个序列中都出现且顺序一致的最长子序列长度，用最大化递推求解。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: LCS is the length of the longest subsequence appearing in the same order in both sequences, solved with a maximizing recurrence.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把一个字符串变成另一个所需要的最少插入、删除、替换次数，用最小化递推求解。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Edit distance is the minimum number of insertions, deletions, and replacements to turn one string into another, solved with a minimizing recurrence.

optionExplanations: “几乎正确”的代码通常语法完全合法，能正常编译运行，不会报错提醒你。
递推选错会直接产生错误的输出数值，这是正确性问题，不只是风格问题。
类型检查只管变量类型对不对，不管数值算法层面的语义是否正确。
edit distance 和 LCS 表格形状几乎一样，但一个求最小代价、一个求最大长度，借错模板依然能跑。
optionExplanations_en: Almost-right code is usually syntactically valid and compiles and runs fine, so nothing warns you at all.
Picking the wrong recurrence produces wrong output values directly — that's correctness, not style.
Type checking only validates variable types; it says nothing about whether the algorithm's logic is right.
Edit distance and LCS share almost the same table shape, but one minimizes cost and the other maximizes length, so borrowing the wrong one still runs.

scenario: 题目只需要“前 i 个物品、容量 j”两维，AI 却给出 `dp[i][j][k]`，面试只剩 10 分钟。
scenario_en: The problem only needs two dimensions, the first i items and capacity j, but the AI returns dp[i][j][k] and only ten minutes are left in the interview.
q: 面对这个解释不了的额外维度，应该怎么处理？
q_en: How should you handle that extra dimension you cannot explain?
options: 把整个二维状态表硬换成一个字符串
让 AI 说清这个维度代表什么；说不清就要求简化状态
直接删掉所有之前已经验证过的 base case
无条件全盘接受，维度越多说明考虑越周全
options_en: Forcibly turn the entire 2D state table into a string.
Ask the AI to justify the dimension's meaning and necessity; simplify the state if it cannot.
Delete all the base cases that were previously verified.
Accept it unconditionally — more dimensions must mean more thorough thinking.
why: 额外维度常是模型在不确定状态时的保守堆叠。你无法解释的维度，就是无法验证的不变量。
why_en: An unexplained DP dimension is a state-design smell that should be justified or removed.
optionExplanations: 把表结构换成字符串完全不回答“这个新维度到底在追踪什么”这个问题。
让 AI 说清新增维度代表什么，能确认它是真实需要还是模型不确定时的保守堆叠，说不清就砍掉。
base case 是递推的根基，删掉后整张表连起点都没有了，这是破坏性的动作。
维度越多状态空间越大，调试和验证只会更难，不会天然更安全。
optionExplanations_en: Swapping the table structure for a string doesn't answer what the new dimension is actually tracking.
Making the AI justify the new dimension tells you if it's genuinely needed or just defensive padding — cut it if it can't explain.
Base cases anchor the recurrence; deleting them leaves the whole table with no starting point at all.
More dimensions mean a larger state space, which only makes debugging and verification harder, not safer.

scenario: 你的状态是“前 i 个元素”，循环需要写到 `i = n`。
scenario_en: Your state means the first i elements, and the loop needs to write through i = n.
q: 这个 DP 数组的大小通常应该是什么？
q_en: What size should this DP array usually be?
options: 固定 1
与输入无关
options_en: A fixed size of 1
n minus 1
n plus 1
Independent of the input
why: 前缀状态通常包含空前缀 `0` 到完整前缀 `n`，所以需要 n+1 个格子。分配 n 个元素再写 dp[n] 会越界。
why_en: Prefix-based states usually need n plus one cells to include the empty prefix and the full prefix.
whenOtherWins: 如果状态定义是“从索引 i 开始”而不是“前 i 个”，大小可能是 n；关键是让数组大小和状态语义一致。
tradeoff: 数组大小 n+1（覆盖空前缀到满前缀）vs 数组大小 n（仅当状态语义是“从 i 开始”时才对）
optionExplanations: 把数组大小写死成常量 1，根本放不下 i 从 0 到 n 的所有状态。
少分配了一格，循环写到 `dp[n]` 时会读写到数组外面去，越界。
状态是“前 i 个元素”，取值从 0（空前缀）到 n（完整），共 n+1 个格子，正好对上。
数组大小恰恰应该由状态定义的取值范围决定，不能说和输入无关。
optionExplanations_en: Hardcoding the size to a constant 1 can't hold all the states for i from 0 through n.
Allocating one cell too few means the loop writing dp[n] reads or writes past the end of the array.
The state is first-i-elements, ranging from 0 (empty) to n (full), which is exactly n+1 cells.
Array size should be exactly determined by the range the state covers, never independent of the input.

scenario: 空串用例挂了，AI 不动 base case，只在函数开头加一行拦截，其他边界都还没测。
scenario_en: The empty-string case fails, and instead of touching the base case the AI just adds a guard line at the top, with the other edge cases still untested.
q: 这种在函数开头硬编码空输入返回值的修法，是什么味道？
q_en: What smell is that hardcoded empty-input return at the top of the function?
options: 这足以说明递推逻辑一定完全正确无误
这说明后续测试都可以完全省略不写
这是业界公认的所有 DP 面试题标准写法
更像是在掩盖 base case 初始化错误
options_en: This is enough to prove the recurrence logic is completely correct.
This means every later test can be skipped entirely.
This is the industry-standard way to write every DP interview solution.
It may be papering over a base-case bug instead of fixing the table's initialization.
why: DP 的边界应和状态表语义一致。硬编码通过一个测试，可能让其他边界继续错。
why_en: A hardcoded edge fix can mask a broken DP base case instead of correcting the state table.
optionExplanations: 通过一个特判测试完全不能证明递推逻辑本身是对的，只是绕开了这一个输入。
单字符、相等字符串这些其他边界仍然可能带着同样的 base case 问题，需要继续测。
标准写法是让 `dp[0]` 或首行首列在表初始化时就正确，而不是在函数入口单独特判。
如果 base case 初始化本身没问题，根本不需要在函数开头额外硬编码这一行，这更像是在掩盖问题。
optionExplanations_en: Passing one special-cased test proves nothing about the recurrence itself — it just routes around that input.
Other edges, like single-character or equal strings, can still carry the same base-case bug and still need testing.
The standard approach initializes dp[0] or the first row/column correctly inside the table, not with an entry guard.
If the base case were actually correct, this hardcoded branch wouldn't be needed — it looks like it's papering over the bug.

scenario: 同一道 DP 题你已经让 AI 重写了三次，每次状态定义都不一样，测试还是红的。
scenario_en: You have had the AI rewrite the same DP problem three times, each with a different state definition, and the tests are still red.
q: AI 编码里说的 “DP spiral”（DP 螺旋）指什么？
q_en: What is the DP spiral in AI-assisted coding?
options: DP 表格在纸上必须严格画成螺旋形状
AI 反复换状态、加维度重写，看似进展却没找到根因
所有 DP 问题都必须用递归调用栈的方式来实现
写的测试数量越少，代码就天然越稳定
options_en: The DP table must strictly be drawn as a spiral shape on paper.
The AI repeatedly swaps states, adds dimensions, and rewrites the approach — looking like progress without ever finding the root cause.
Every DP problem must be implemented with a recursive call stack.
The fewer tests you write, the more inherently stable the code becomes.
why: 第三次生成如果比第二次完全不同，通常不是进展，而是失控。应停下来重新定义状态或自己写关键几行。
why_en: A DP spiral is uncontrolled rewriting of state and dimensions instead of fixing the specific bug.
optionExplanations: 这个说法和表格怎么在纸上画完全无关，它是一个调试失控的比喻。
AI 一次次换状态、加维度、重写方案，看起来在动但没有真的定位到那个具体的 bug。
自底向上 tabulation 完全不用递归，DP 的实现方式本来就不止一种。
测试写得少只会让你更晚才发现 bug，并不会让代码本身更稳定。
optionExplanations_en: This term has nothing to do with how the table is drawn — it's a metaphor for debugging going out of control.
The AI keeps swapping states, adding dimensions, and rewriting — it looks like motion but never pins down the bug.
Bottom-up tabulation uses no recursion at all, so DP has more than one valid implementation style.
Writing fewer tests only delays when you discover a bug — it doesn't make the code any more stable.

scenario: 题目要求列出所有和为 k 的子集，而不是只问有多少种或最优值。
scenario_en: The problem asks you to list all subsets that sum to k, not just count them or find one optimal value.
q: 更自然的起点是什么？
q_en: What is the more natural starting point?
options: Dijkstra
LRU Cache
只返回一个 DP 数字
回溯枚举所有合法子集
options_en: Dijkstra's algorithm
An LRU cache
Return a single DP number
Backtracking to enumerate every valid subset
why: “列出所有”通常要求保留每个具体解，回溯更直接。DP 可用于计数或可行性，也可和回溯结合，但不是默认替代。
why_en: Enumerating every valid subset is naturally backtracking, while DP is better for counts or optimal values.
whenOtherWins: 如果题目只问可行性或方案数，且重复状态明显，DP 会更高效。
tradeoff: 枚举所有具体解（回溯）vs 只求一个最优值或方案数（DP）

termDefinitions.meaning: 系统地尝试、递归深入、遇到不满足条件就撤销选择的搜索方式，能枚举所有合法解。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Backtracking systematically tries choices, recurses deeper, and undoes a choice when it fails, enumerating every valid solution.

termDefinitions.meaning: 求带权图中单源最短路径的经典算法。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Dijkstra's algorithm finds the shortest paths from a single source in a weighted graph.

optionExplanations: Dijkstra 求的是带权图里的最短路径，这里没有图也没有边权，无从下手。
LRU 管的是缓存该淘汰谁，和枚举所有满足条件的子集完全无关。
题目要的是“列出所有子集”，一个 DP 数字压缩掉了每个具体解的内容，答不了这个要求。
系统地尝试、遇到不满足就撤销选择，每条走到底的路径正好对应一个具体子集，天然能保留所有解。
optionExplanations_en: Dijkstra finds shortest paths in a weighted graph; there's no graph or edge weights here to run it on.
An LRU cache decides what to evict from memory, unrelated to enumerating every qualifying subset.
The task asks to list every subset; a single DP number collapses away each solution's content, so it can't satisfy that.
Trying a choice and undoing it when it fails means each completed path corresponds to one specific subset.

scenario: 输入规模 n ≤ 20，暴力枚举 2ⁿ 个子集能在时间内跑完，且 DP 状态设计复杂。
scenario_en: The input size is n <= 20, brute-force enumeration of 2^n subsets fits the time limit, and the DP state is complicated.
q: 合理的工程选择是什么？
q_en: What is the reasonable engineering choice?
options: 先用暴力或回溯，更简单也更好验证
只写一个正则表达式
干脆放弃写任何测试
无条件直接上复杂的 DP 状态
options_en: Start with brute force or backtracking — simpler and easier to verify.
Just write a single regex pattern.
Skip writing any tests at all.
Reach for a complex DP state unconditionally, no matter what.
why: DP 以状态设计复杂度换取性能。输入足够小且暴力可验证时，不必为了模式而上模式。
why_en: For tiny inputs, brute force can be the better engineering choice because it is simpler and easier to verify.
whenOtherWins: 如果输入上限变大或隐藏测试会压性能，再转向 DP 或剪枝优化。
tradeoff: n≤20 时暴力枚举（简单、易验证、O(2ⁿ)可接受）vs 复杂 DP（状态设计成本高，收益在小输入下不明显）
optionExplanations: n≤20 时 2ⁿ 顶多百万级别，暴力枚举跑得动，实现和验证都比设计复杂状态简单。
正则解决的是模式匹配，答不了“枚举所有满足和为 k 的子集”这类组合问题。
没有测试，无论是暴力实现还是以后的 DP 实现，都没法确认是否正确。
输入已经小到暴力可行时还硬上复杂 DP，是不必要的工程投入，还多了出错的地方。
optionExplanations_en: With n at most 20, 2 to the n is at most about a million — brute force runs fine and is simpler to verify.
Regex solves pattern matching, not combinatorial tasks like enumerating every subset that sums to k.
Without tests, there's no way to confirm either the brute-force or a future DP version is correct.
Reaching for a complex DP when brute force already fits is unnecessary effort with more places to get it wrong.

scenario: 状态之间天然形成一个图，题目问最短步数或可达性，状态转移很清晰。
scenario_en: The states naturally form a graph, the problem asks for shortest steps or reachability, and the transitions are clear.
q: 除了 DP，还应考虑什么？
q_en: What should you consider besides DP?
options: 手写一个 LRU 缓存淘汰策略
把候选按字母顺序排序
只用一个双向链表结构
BFS/Dijkstra 图搜索
options_en: Hand-writing an LRU cache eviction policy
Sorting the candidates alphabetically
Using only a doubly linked list structure
Graph search such as BFS or Dijkstra
why: 一些问题可建成状态图，最短路径或可达性用图搜索更容易向 AI 说明和验证。不要把所有状态转移题都强行 DP 化。
why_en: When states form a natural graph and the question is reachability or shortest path, graph search may be cleaner than DP.
whenOtherWins: 如果状态有明确拓扑顺序并且要聚合最优值，DP 表或 DAG 上 DP 可能更直接。
tradeoff: 状态天然是图、求最短路/可达性（图搜索更直接）vs 状态需要聚合最优值且有拓扑序（DP 更直接）

termDefinitions.meaning: 广度优先搜索：按层扩展，是无权图求最短步数的标准算法。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: BFS expands layer by layer and is the standard algorithm for shortest steps in an unweighted graph.

termDefinitions.meaning: 求带权图中单源最短路径的经典算法。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Dijkstra's algorithm finds the shortest paths from a single source in a weighted graph.

termDefinitions.meaning: 有向无环图：节点间有方向且没有环，天然给出可用于 DP 的拓扑顺序。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A DAG is a directed graph with no cycles, which naturally provides a topological order usable for DP.

optionExplanations: LRU 是缓存淘汰策略，和求最短步数或可达性完全无关。
按字母排序不会告诉你从起点到终点最少要走几步。
双向链表只是一种容器，本身不携带节点之间该怎么转移的信息。
状态天然形成图时，BFS 求无权最短步数、Dijkstra 求带权最短路径，都比硬套 DP 更直接。
optionExplanations_en: An LRU cache is an eviction policy, entirely unrelated to shortest steps or reachability.
Sorting alphabetically tells you nothing about the minimum number of steps from start to end.
A doubly linked list is just a container; it carries no information about how nodes transition.
When states naturally form a graph, BFS for shortest steps or Dijkstra for shortest paths beats forcing a DP table.

scenario: AI 编码面试里，面试官默认 AI 写得出 DP 代码，评分看你怎么驱动它和验证它的输出。
scenario_en: In an AI coding interview the interviewer assumes the AI can write DP code, so the score comes from how you drive it and verify its output.
q: DP 题中，哪些行为是强信号？
q_en: Which behaviors are strong signals in a DP interview problem?
options: 用 DP 术语说出状态、递推、base cases
手推或打印表格验证 AI 的递推
能解释为什么是二维而不是一维
测试失败后沉默地让 AI 一直重写
options_en: Naming the state, recurrence, and base cases out loud in DP vocabulary.
Hand-tracing or printing the table to verify the AI's recurrence.
Being able to explain why the table is 2D instead of 1D.
Silently letting the AI keep rewriting after a test fails.
why: 面试官知道 AI 能写 DP 代码，真正要看你是否能指向正确状态并验证输出。失控重写是负信号。
why_en: Strong DP signals are naming the state and recurrence, verifying the table, and defending dimensionality.
optionExplanations: 写代码前先用一句话说清状态、递推来源和边界，是面试官判断你是否真的设计了方案的第一信号。
拿一个具体小例子核对 AI 表格里的数字，能把藏在循环里的 bug 变成可观察的证据。
能说清为什么状态要两维而不是压成一维，证明你理解语义，不是照抄了一个看着对的模板。
测试失败时既不形成假设也不介入，只是反复让 AI 重来，会让面试官怀疑你没在主导调试。
optionExplanations_en: Stating the state, recurrence, and boundaries in one sentence before coding is the first signal an interviewer grades.
Checking the AI's table numbers against a small concrete example turns a hidden loop bug into observable evidence.
Explaining why the state needs two dimensions instead of one proves you understand it, not just copied a template.
Forming no hypothesis and letting the AI retry endlessly makes the interviewer doubt you're directing the debugging.

q: 把 AI 编码面试中的 DP 工作流按顺序排列。
q_en: Put the DP workflow for an AI coding interview in order.
steps: 让 AI 生成 bottom-up 或 memoized 实现。
识别产品包装下的 DP 模式。
用测试、手推格子或打印表格验证输出。
用一句话定义状态，并说出 base cases。
先写几个小测试，尤其是边界输入。
why: 先识别和定义状态，再用测试约束实现，最后验证。这个流程把最容易错的边界放在 AI 写代码之前。
why_en: The DP interview loop is recognize, define state and bases, write tests, generate code, and verify the table.
tradeoff: 先定状态和测试再生成代码（多几分钟但可验证）vs 直接生成代码再补救（省时间但容易在错的方案上调试）

scenario: 你要在提示 AI 之前先手推一个具体例子，既验证自己理解了编辑语义，又能把它变成后续的自动化测试用例。
scenario_en: Before prompting the AI, you want to hand-work a concrete example that checks your edit semantics and later becomes an automated test.
q: 填空：文章中的 edit distance 手算例子。
q_en: Fill in the article's hand-worked edit-distance example.
text: `KATE` 变成 `SAT` 至少需要 {{2}} 次编辑：先把 K 替换成 S，再删除末尾的 E。
why: 手推公式：替换 1 次 + 删除 1 次 = 2 次编辑，这个数字直接变成测试用例 `edit_distance('kate','sat') == 2`，是后续验证 AI 代码表格是否正确的基准。
why_en: KATE to SAT has edit distance two, making it a useful hand-checkable DP test.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把一个字符串变成另一个所需要的最少插入、删除、替换次数。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Edit distance is the minimum number of insertions, deletions, and replacements needed to turn one string into another.

scenario: AI 写了一个前缀 DP，你需要快速检查 loop 边界和 return cell 是否匹配状态。
scenario_en: The AI wrote a prefix DP, and you need to quickly check whether the loop bounds and return cell match the state.
q: 下面哪项最符合 `dp[i][j]` 表示两个前缀完整消耗后的返回？
q_en: Which return cell best matches dp[i][j] after both prefixes are fully consumed?
codeSample:
m, n = len(s), len(t)
dp = [[0] * (n + 1) for _ in range(m + 1)]
# fill table...
return ???
options: dp[n][m] 一定正确
dp[m][n]
options_en: dp[n][m] is always correct.
dp[m][n]
why: 如果状态包含空前缀到完整前缀，完整字符串对应 `m` 和 `n`。返回 `m-1,n-1` 是典型 off-by-one。
why_en: For prefix lengths including zero, the full strings live at dp[m][n].
whenOtherWins: 如果状态定义用真实字符索引而不是前缀长度，返回位置可能不同；必须回到状态语义判断。
tradeoff: return cell 由状态语义决定（dp[m][n] 对应两个前缀长度）vs 想当然套用行列互换或减一的写法
optionExplanations: 数组是 m+1 行、n+1 列，行列对调后 `dp[n][m]` 大概率越界或读到错的格子。
数组按 s 的长度 m 做行、t 的长度 n 做列声明，两个字符串都消耗完正好落在 `dp[m][n]`。
`dp[0][0]` 是两个空前缀的起点，是还没开始比较的地方，不是最终答案。
完整字符串对应下标 m 和 n，`m-1,n-1` 少读了一个字符，是典型的少一格。
optionExplanations_en: The array has m+1 rows and n+1 columns; swapping them means dp[n][m] likely goes out of bounds.
The array is declared with s's length m as rows and t's length n as columns, so full strings land at dp[m][n].
dp[0][0] is the starting point with two empty prefixes, before any comparison — not the final answer.
The full strings sit at indices m and n; dp[m-1][n-1] reads one character short, a classic off-by-one.

scenario: 两个字符串长度分别为 m 和 n，你在检查 AI 声明的前缀 DP 数组大小是否正确。
scenario_en: The two strings have lengths m and n, and you are checking whether the AI declared the prefix DP table with the right size.
q: 为什么前缀 DP 表格通常要开成 `(m + 1) x (n + 1)`，而不是 `m x n`？
q_en: Why is a prefix DP table usually (m + 1) by (n + 1), not m by n?
options: 因为 n 和 m 总是相等
因为答案需要两个副本
因为 Python 数组必须多一行
要包含空前缀行和空前缀列
options_en: Because n and m are always equal.
Because the answer needs two copies.
Because Python arrays must always have one extra row.
To include the row and column for the empty prefix.
why: 空前缀（长度 0）是合法的起始子问题，公式是行数=m+1、列数=n+1，覆盖 0..m 和 0..n 两个前缀长度区间。少这一行列会导致 base case 无处安放、后续所有格子索引错位。
why_en: Prefix DP tables add one row and column to represent empty prefixes.
optionExplanations: 两个字符串长度完全没理由总是相等，题目也没有这个假设。
答案是表格里的一个格子，不需要“两个副本”这种说法。
多一行列是状态语义决定的，跟用什么语言实现没有关系。
边界情况是「一个字符串还没开始比较」，这也算一种状态，所以行列数都要比长度多算一格。
optionExplanations_en: There's no reason the two string lengths must always be equal, and the problem never assumes that.
The answer is one cell in the table; there's no such thing as needing two copies of it.
The extra row and column come from the state's semantics, not from any quirk of the language used.
An empty prefix (length 0) is a legitimate starting subproblem, so m+1 rows and n+1 columns cover 0..m and 0..n.

scenario: 你只有一周准备 AI 编码面试，目标是练识别与状态定义，而不是练手写代码速度。
scenario_en: You have one week to prepare for an AI coding interview, and the goal is recognition and state definition, not handwriting code faster.
q: 为了训练 DP 识别力，应该练哪些形状的题？
q_en: Which shapes of problems should you practice to train DP recognition?
options: House Robber 这种一维 DP
Unique Paths 这种二维表
Word Break 这种不那么显然的状态
Maximum Profit in Job Scheduling 这种排序 + 二分 + DP
options_en: House Robber, a one-dimensional DP
Unique Paths, a two-dimensional table
Word Break, whose state is less obvious
Maximum Profit in Job Scheduling, which combines sorting, binary search, and DP
why: 练习目标不是打字速度，而是识别包装、定义状态、写测试和验证输出。不同形状能覆盖不同状态设计。
why_en: Practicing varied DP shapes trains recognition and state definition rather than implementation speed.
optionExplanations: House Robber 是典型一维 DP，练的是“相邻决策互斥”这类状态设计。
Unique Paths 是典型二维表，练的是两个维度共同决定一个格子该怎么转移。
Word Break 的状态不那么直白，练的是从包装文字里抽出“能不能切分”这种非显然状态。
Maximum Profit in Job Scheduling 把排序、二分和 DP 组合在一起，练的是多个技巧叠加的识别能力。
optionExplanations_en: House Robber is a classic 1D DP that trains recognizing an adjacent-choices-conflict state.
Unique Paths is a classic 2D table that trains how two dimensions jointly determine a cell's transition.
Word Break has a less obvious state, training you to pull a can-it-be-split state out of wordy phrasing.
Maximum Profit in Job Scheduling stacks sorting, binary search, and DP, training multi-technique recognition.

scenario: 同一道爬楼梯题，一份解法是递归加 memo，一份是自底向上填表，你要说清它们本质上共享什么。
scenario_en: For the same climbing-stairs problem, one solution is recursion with memoization and the other is bottom-up tabulation, and you need to say what they fundamentally share.
q: memoization 和 bottom-up tabulation 的共同点是什么？
q_en: What do memoization and bottom-up tabulation have in common?
options: 都必须使用二维数组
都不需要 base case
都不能处理字符串
都保证每个不同子问题只计算一次
options_en: Both must use a 2D array.
Neither needs base cases.
Neither can handle strings.
Both guarantee each distinct subproblem is computed only once.
why: memo 是递归时缓存；tabulation 是从小到大填表。形式不同，但目的都是复用子问题答案。
why_en: Memoization and tabulation both avoid recomputing the same subproblem.
tradeoff: memoization：递归 + 缓存，写起来更接近暴力递归，但有调用栈开销 vs tabulation：显式循环填表，无栈开销，但要自己想清楚遍历顺序

termDefinitions.meaning: 递归时把已经算过的子问题结果存起来，下次遇到直接返回缓存值。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Memoization stores the result of a subproblem the first time it is computed and returns the cached value on repeat calls.

termDefinitions.meaning: 自底向上填表：从最小的子问题开始，按依赖顺序逐个算到目标状态。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Tabulation fills a table bottom-up, computing each state in dependency order from the smallest subproblem to the target.

optionExplanations: 数组维度由状态本身决定，一维、二维、三维都能用这两种技巧实现，不是它们的限制。
两者都仍然需要 base case：memo 靠它终止递归，tabulation 靠它当填表起点。
edit distance、LCS 这类字符串 DP 正是这两种技巧最常见的应用场景之一。
memo 靠递归加缓存、tabulation 靠按序填表，路径不同但都保证每个不同状态只算一次。
optionExplanations_en: Array dimensionality comes from the state design itself; both work fine at 1D, 2D, or 3D — it's not a limit of either.
Both still need base cases: memoization uses them to stop recursion, tabulation uses them as starting values.
String DP problems like edit distance and LCS are among the most common uses of both techniques.
Memoization uses recursion plus a cache while tabulation fills in order — different paths, same one-compute-per-state result.

scenario: DP 表的每一行只依赖上一行，你已经有正确的二维版本并通过测试。
scenario_en: Each DP table row only depends on the previous row, and you already have a correct 2D version that passes tests.
q: 什么时候才应该让 AI 做滚动数组优化？
q_en: When should you ask the AI to optimize with a rolling array?
options: 测试失败时用滚动数组掩盖问题
一开始就优化，哪怕状态和递推还没定义清楚
永远不要优化
确认正确性后，且空间约束或输入规模需要时
options_en: Use a rolling array to paper over a failing test.
Optimize from the very start, even before the state and recurrence are defined.
Never optimize at all.
Only after correctness is confirmed, and only when memory constraints or input size justify it.
why: 先有可读可验证版本，再优化空间。滚动数组会增加索引复杂度，不应该用来替代正确性验证。
why_en: Space optimization should come after the clear DP version is correct and memory pressure justifies it.
whenOtherWins: 如果面试明确要求 O(1) 或 O(n) 空间，可以较早讨论滚动数组，但仍要先说清依赖关系。
tradeoff: 先正确后优化（二维表更易调试，滚动数组延后）vs 一开始就滚动数组（省内存但索引更难验证，容易掩盖 bug）
optionExplanations: 拿滚动数组去掩盖一个还没定位的测试失败，只会让索引更难读，根因更难找。
状态本身都还没验证清楚就急着压缩空间，优化后的代码只是更难调试的错误代码。
有些面试明确要求 O(1) 或 O(n) 空间，完全拒绝优化会答不到点上。
先在二维表上核对手推例子和测试，确认递推、base case 全对，再按空间需要压缩，风险最可控。
optionExplanations_en: Reaching for a rolling array to hide an undiagnosed failing test just makes indices harder to read.
Rushing to compress space before the state is verified just turns wrong code into harder-to-debug wrong code.
Some interviews explicitly require O(1) or O(n) space, so refusing to optimize at all misses the point.
Verify the recurrence and base cases on the 2D table first, then compress only if space demands it.

scenario: 你审查 AI 写的 edit distance，发现相等字符分支仍然加 1。
scenario_en: You are reviewing AI-written edit distance code and notice that the equal-character branch still adds 1.
q: 应该怎么判断这个 bug？
q_en: How should you judge this bug?
options: 应该直接删除整个 dp 表格然后重写
应该把整个算法改成用拓扑排序来解决
相等字符不需要编辑，应改成 `dp[i-1][j-1]`
这是正确写法，因为比较字符本身也应该算作一次编辑代价
options_en: Delete the entire dp table and rewrite it from scratch.
Change the whole algorithm to use topological sort instead.
Matching characters need no edit, so it should be dp[i-1][j-1].
This is correct, because comparing characters itself should also count as an edit cost.
why: 编辑距离只计插入、删除、替换。字符已经匹配时不付成本，直接继承左上角。
why_en: A matching character should copy the diagonal without adding an edit cost.
whenOtherWins: 如果问题定义给匹配也设置成本，那递推会不同；标准 edit distance 没有这个成本。
tradeoff: 匹配字符复制左上角（标准 edit distance，零代价）vs 匹配字符也加 1（非标准变体，需求里明确才这么定义）
optionExplanations: 删掉整张表重写是无关且破坏性的动作，丢掉了已经写对的边界和大部分递推，根本没定位到问题。
拓扑排序解决的是有向图节点排序问题，和这里的字符比较 bug 毫无关系。
字符已经匹配就不该再计一次编辑，去掉多余的 `1 +`，让它直接继承左上角格子即可。
标准编辑距离只统计插入、删除、替换三种操作，单纯字符相等的比较本身不算一次编辑。
optionExplanations_en: Deleting the whole table and starting over is destructive and throws away base cases that were already right.
Topological sort orders nodes in a directed graph; it has nothing to do with this character-comparison bug.
A matching character shouldn't cost anything — drop the extra 1 + so the cell simply inherits the diagonal.
Standard edit distance counts only insert, delete, and replace; comparing equal characters is never an edit.

scenario: AI 写的 edit distance 表格逐格核对都对，但它返回 `dp[n-1][m-1]`，样例结果偏小 1。
scenario_en: The AI edit-distance table checks out cell by cell, but it returns dp[n-1][m-1] and the sample result is off by one.
q: DP 代码审查里，为什么 return cell 是单独检查项？
q_en: Why is the return cell a separate check in DP code review?
options: return cell 这一行的写法会直接改变递推公式本身
表格可能填对了，但返回了错误状态或 off-by-one 位置
return cell 这一行永远不可能写错
只要写好了测试，就完全不需要再检查它
options_en: How this return-cell line is written directly changes the recurrence formula itself.
The table may be filled correctly but still return the wrong state or an off-by-one position.
The return-cell line can never be written incorrectly.
As long as tests are written, it never needs to be checked again.
why: 状态语义决定答案在哪个格子。返回错格子会让大部分代码看起来正确，却输出相邻子问题的答案。
why_en: The return cell matters because a correct table can still return the wrong subproblem.
optionExplanations: return 语句只是读取一个格子，不参与循环里 `dp[i][j]` 本身的计算过程。
填表和返回是两个独立步骤：表格可能全对，但 `return dp[m-1][n-1]` 这类写法会取到相邻子问题而不是答案。
return cell 上的少一格错误其实非常常见，尤其是前缀长度和索引混淆的时候。
如果测试用例恰好没覆盖这个边界，错误的返回位置照样能蒙混过关，光靠测试不够。
optionExplanations_en: The return statement only reads a cell; it plays no role in computing dp[i][j] inside the loop itself.
Filling the table and returning a cell are separate steps: the table can be right while return dp[m-1][n-1] reads a neighbor.
Off-by-one mistakes in the return cell are actually very common when prefix length and index get confused.
If the tests happen not to cover this edge, a wrong return position can slip through — tests alone aren't enough.

q: 填空：好的 DP 状态应该先是什么样子？
q_en: Fill in what a good DP state should look like first.
text: 好的 DP 状态先是一句清楚的{{语义描述}}，例如“`dp[i][j]` 表示前 i 个物品、预算 j 下的最优值”，然后才是代码里的数组。
why: 如果你说不出格子的含义，就无法判断递推、base case 和返回值是否正确。状态定义是人类不能完全外包的部分。
why_en: A DP state should first be a clear semantic sentence, not just an array declaration.

scenario: 你拿不准题目是不是 DP，就问模型“这题看起来像 DP 吗”；同一段题面换成“像贪心吗”，它同样点头。
scenario_en: Unsure whether the problem is DP, you ask the model "does this look like DP?" — and when you re-ask the same prompt as "does this look greedy?", it agrees with that too.
q: 为什么模式识别这一步不能交给模型拍板？
q_en: Why is naming the pattern the one step you cannot let the model decide?
options: 模型会附和你给的任何框架，拿不到独立判断
模型的算法知识不足以理解 edit distance 这类模式
模型对超过一千字的题面会拒绝作答
模型必须先看到测试用例才能识别模式
options_en: The model agrees with whatever framing you give it, so you get no independent judgement.
The model does not know enough algorithms to understand patterns like edit distance.
The model refuses to answer once the problem statement passes a thousand words.
The model can only recognize a pattern after it has seen the test cases.
why: 模型的附和倾向让它对任一框架都点头；而面试官打分的正是你自己出声点名模式并且点对。
why_en: The model will agree with any framing you hand it, so recognition has to be your call — that is exactly what the interviewer is grading.

termDefinitions.meaning: 动态规划：把问题拆成重叠子问题，用状态和递推复用已算过的答案。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Dynamic programming breaks a problem into overlapping subproblems and reuses answers already computed.

termDefinitions.meaning: 附和倾向：模型倾向于顺着你给的框架点头，而不是给出独立判断。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Sycophancy is the model’s tendency to agree with whatever framing you hand it instead of judging independently.

termDefinitions.meaning: 编辑距离：把一个字符串改成另一个所需的最少单字符插入、删除、替换次数。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Edit distance is the minimum number of single-character inserts, deletes, and replaces that turn one string into another.

termDefinitions.meaning: 贪心算法：每步都选当前看起来最优的选项，不回头验证。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A greedy algorithm always takes the option that looks best right now and never revisits it.

optionExplanations: 换个框架问它就换个答案，等于你自己的判断被复读了一遍。
模型写这类递推很熟，问题出在它不替你做取舍，不是知识不够。
题面长度不是限制；模糊的是判断责任归属，不是输入容量。
识别是在写测试之前做的判断，等测试出来就已经晚了。
optionExplanations_en: Change the framing and it changes its answer — it just echoes your own guess back at you.
The model writes these recurrences fluently; the gap is judgement, not algorithmic knowledge.
Prompt length is not the limit here — what is unclear is who owns the call.
Recognition happens before you write tests; waiting for them is already too late.

scenario: 面试官追问“为什么是 dp[i][j] 不是 dp[i]”。这题要把字符串 s 改写成 t，两条序列各要一个下标往前走。
scenario_en: The interviewer asks why you used dp[i][j] instead of dp[i]. The problem rewrites string s into string t, and each of the two sequences needs its own index walking forward.
q: DP 状态该开几维，由什么决定？
q_en: What decides how many dimensions a DP state needs?
options: 由定位一个子问题需要几个独立索引决定
由输入字符串的最大长度是否超过一千决定
由 AI 生成的数组声明写了几层中括号决定
由时间复杂度目标是 O(n) 还是 O(n²) 决定
options_en: By how many independent indices it takes to pin down one subproblem.
By whether the longest input string goes past a thousand characters.
By how many bracket levels the model happened to write in the array declaration.
By whether you are targeting O(n) or O(n squared) time.
why: 两条序列各要定位自己的前缀，就得有两个下标；维数是状态语义的结果。代价：每多一维就多一层循环和一整维内存。
why_en: Two sequences means two prefixes to pin down, so two indices — dimensionality falls out of the state sentence, and each extra dimension costs another loop and another axis of memory.
whenOtherWins: 如果一个位置就能定位子问题（爬楼梯、house robber 这类单序列题），一维 dp[i] 就够，硬开二维只是白烧内存。
tradeoff: 一维 dp[i]：状态少、内存小 vs 二维 dp[i][j]：能同时定位两条序列的前缀

termDefinitions.meaning: 动态规划：把问题拆成重叠子问题，用状态和递推复用已算过的答案。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Dynamic programming breaks a problem into overlapping subproblems and reuses answers already computed.

termDefinitions.meaning: 编辑距离：把一个字符串改成另一个所需的最少单字符插入、删除、替换次数。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Edit distance is the minimum number of single-character inserts, deletes, and replaces that turn one string into another.

optionExplanations: “前 i 个字符改成前 j 个字符”这句话里有几个索引，表就开几维。
规模只影响能不能跑得完，不影响一个格子代表什么。
括号层数是模型的输出结果，反过来当依据就是让它替你定状态。
复杂度是维数和转移的结果，不能倒过来当维数的选择依据。
optionExplanations_en: Count the indices in the sentence "the first i characters into the first j" — that is your dimension count.
Input size affects whether it finishes in time, not what a single cell means.
Bracket depth is the model’s output; using it as your reason hands the state decision to it.
Complexity follows from the dimensions and transitions, so it cannot be the reason for picking them.

scenario: 你只说了一句“implement edit distance”，状态、维度、base case 全由模型挑；面试官从头到尾只看到模型的产出。
scenario_en: You said only "implement edit distance" — the model picked the state, the dimensions, and the base cases, and the interviewer watched nothing but the model’s output.
q: 除了你答不上追问，这种提示还有什么深层代价？
q_en: Beyond being unable to answer follow-ups, what does a prompt this thin cost you?
options: 面试官实际在给模型打分，并默认是模型救了你
模型会因为提示太短而退化成明显更慢的暴力实现
模型会拒绝执行没有写明 base case 的提示
这只影响代码可读性，评价结果不受影响
options_en: The interviewer ends up grading the model, and defaults to assuming it bailed you out.
A prompt that short makes the model fall back to a much slower brute-force implementation.
The model will refuse a prompt that does not spell out the base cases.
It only affects how readable the code is; the evaluation itself is unchanged.
why: 设计不在你手里时，面试官看不到你的判断、只看得到模型的产出，无从分辨你懂还是它救场，就默认是后者。
why_en: With no design coming from you, the interviewer can only see the model’s output — they cannot tell whether you understood it or it bailed you out, so they assume the latter.

termDefinitions.meaning: 动态规划：把问题拆成重叠子问题，用状态和递推复用已算过的答案。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Dynamic programming breaks a problem into overlapping subproblems and reuses answers already computed.

termDefinitions.meaning: 编辑距离：把一个字符串改成另一个所需的最少单字符插入、删除、替换次数。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Edit distance is the minimum number of single-character inserts, deletes, and replaces that turn one string into another.

termDefinitions.meaning: 基准情形：不靠递推、直接写死答案的最小子问题，如空串到空串是 0。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A base case is the smallest subproblem whose answer you write down directly instead of deriving it.

optionExplanations: 你的判断没有留下任何可观察的痕迹，评分只能落到模型头上。
模型多半照样给出教科书递推，问题不在慢，在这个选择不是你做的。
模糊提示不会被拒绝，它会替你挑一个默认值，这才是麻烦所在。
这一轮评的是判断力，不是排版，代价直接落在结论上。
optionExplanations_en: Your judgement leaves no observable trace, so the only thing left to grade is the model.
It will usually still emit the textbook recurrence — the issue is not speed, it is that the choice was not yours.

两条路各写一版，用测试挑跑得更快的那一版

Build the full DP table first, then simplify it back down to greedy.
Write both versions and let the tests pick whichever runs faster.
Look at input size and always jump straight to DP once n gets large.

把选择树建成图，改用 Dijkstra 跑最短路
回溯和 DP 互斥，必须二选一走到底
先跑完整回溯，事后再对结果排序去重

Turn the choice tree into a graph and run Dijkstra for a shortest path.
Backtracking and DP are mutually exclusive; commit to one and stay there.
Run the full backtracking first, then sort and dedupe the results afterwards.

这段是模型写的，我先整体信它一次
我先逐行读一遍循环里的所有索引

why_en: Saying your verification strategy out loud frames everything that follows as deliberate checking rather than hand-waving — and it commits you to actually doing the hand-trace and the tests.
whenOtherWins: 如果函数只有十来行、递推你完全熟，直接读循环边界和返回格更快，不必先铺陈一套策略。

scenario: 面试官出了最长递增子序列 LIS，n 只有几千，朴素平方做法跑得完；他明说想看你怎么定义状态并验证输出。
scenario_en: The interviewer gives you longest increasing subsequence with n only a few thousand, well within reach of the quadratic solution, and says they want to see how you define the state and verify the output.
q: 你该先交出哪一版实现？
q_en: Which implementation should you produce first?
options: 朴素 O(n²) 的 dp[i] 版本
直接上 O(n log n) 的二分优化版本
先枚举全部子序列，再筛出递增的那些
把序列建成图，跑一次最短路算法
options_en: The naive quadratic dp[i] version.
Go straight to the O(n log n) binary-search version.
Enumerate every subsequence first, then filter the increasing ones.
Model the sequence as a graph and run a shortest-path algorithm.
why: n 只有几千时平方做法跑得完，而它的状态一句话就说得清；面试官要的是那句话，不是更快的实现。
why_en: At n in the low thousands the quadratic version finishes fine and its state fits in one sentence — and that sentence is what the interviewer is after, not raw speed.
whenOtherWins: 如果 n 涨到十万级、平方做法跑不完，就得上 O(n log n) 的二分版本，并向面试官解释那个数组维护的是什么。
tradeoff: 朴素 O(n²)：状态一句话说清、好验证 vs O(n log n) 二分：更快，但状态语义绕、更难当场讲明白

termDefinitions.meaning: 最长递增子序列：一个序列里保持递增的最长子序列长度。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The longest increasing subsequence is the longest subsequence of a sequence whose values keep increasing.

optionExplanations: “以第 i 个元素结尾的最长递增长度”这句话可以直接说出口。
它维护的数组不是答案本身，讲清语义要花掉你验证的时间。
子序列有 2ⁿ 个，几千的规模下这条路根本跑不完。
最短路要的是边权语义，这题求的是最长链，套不上去。
optionExplanations_en: You can say "the longest increasing run ending at index i" out loud, and that is the whole state.
The array it maintains is not the answer itself, and explaining that eats the time you need for verification.
There are two-to-the-n subsequences, so at a few thousand elements this never finishes.
Shortest path needs edge-weight semantics, and this asks for a longest chain instead.
